transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-02-11
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Elena Morris (Redwood SE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood CSM), Maya Chen (Lyra CTO), Aaron Li (Lyra ML Eng), Jasmine Park (Lyra PM), Omar Hassan (Lyra Infra)

Auto-summary (auto-gen): Redwood lab runs show median latency improvement ~18-22% on short sequences, throughput 1.4-1.8x vs incumbent on burst paths; p95 varied with long sequence (1.1x to 0.9x).

00:00 Samir: Hey everyone thanks for hopping on, we have about 45 minutes, want to run through the bench results from last week and then go to tuning and next steps. Maya, thanks for making time.
00:12 Maya: yeah thanks, we just want to see the numbers and uh understand the risk for canary, right. We can't have regressions on tail latency during peak traffic.
00:22 Samir: totally understood, that's our priority too. Elena will walk the lab runs and then we can dig into the p95/p99.
00:30 Elena: ok so quick context — we ran the same sample traces you shared, Aaron, across the incumbent cluster and our dedicated test instance. We ran three seq length profiles: short (avg 32 tokens), medium (avg 128) and long (avg 512). For each we measured p50/p95/p99, throughput at target concurrency, and median cost per token using our quantized runner.
00:55 Aaron: quick q, the quantized runner — that's your 4-bit path? any quality diffs we should know?
01:02 Elena: yes it's int4 path for this workload. We did a small eval set — no meaningful quality drift on the classification probes you sent, but full eval will be in the follow-up. Those details are in the spreadsheet.
01:15 Jasmine: can you speak to the cache settings? your notes say prefix cache at 20% hit — is that realistic?
01:22 Elena: good callout. In lab the prefix/KV hit varied by workload. For the short seq profiles we saw higher prefix reuse near 35-40%. For chatty sessions the KV hit was lower. For the runs we presented we used the real trace-derived hit rates to avoid optimistic assumptions.
01:40 Diego: i'll add that our Optimize advisor suggested raising microbatching at the 128 token path to reduce per-token cost w/o hurting p95 — that's the config used for medium profile.
01:49 01:51 Maya: ok lets see numbers please
01:52 Elena: sharing screen — slide 1: short seq (32). p50 incumbent 48ms, redwood 36ms. p95 incumbent 210ms, redwood 165ms. throughput @50 concurrent: incumbent 750 rps, redwood 1,100 rps. cost per 1k tokens: incumbent $0.86, redwood $0.94.
02:24 Aaron: so cost is higher for you on that path but latency is better — our ops team will flag the cost delta, we are sensitive.
02:31 Samir: understood — that delta is mostly due to dedicated GPU footprint for very low-latency paths. We can show a hybrid config that uses smaller instances for low-latency and a cheaper quantized variant for bulk inferencing — tradeoffs and a routing policy.
02:45 Jasmine: medium seq?
02:47 Elena: medium (128) p50 incumbent 220ms, redwood 175ms. p95 incumbent 580ms, redwood 520ms. throughput incumbent 240 rps, redwood 420 rps. cost per 1k tokens incumbent $0.62, redwood $0.58.
03:12 Maya: interesting — cost parity there and much better throughput. why is p95 still relatively close?
03:20 Elena: the tail is influenced by KV cache misses and long-context attention spikes. For the medium profile we saw some model-specific attention cost that kicks in at ~300 tokens due to chunking in the incumbent runtime, which causes head-of-line janking. Our kernel selection smooths that but when cache miss rate spikes, the tail converges.
03:40 Aaron: can you quantify the KV miss vs compute? like what portion of tail is network/serialization vs pure matmul?
03:48 Elena: from flame graphs: approx 60% compute, 25% KV fetch and 15% serialization/dispatch for the medium runs. With our in-process KV caching that drops to 10% fetch when hit rates are high.
04:05 Omar: are those KV calls over the network? in our infra we prefer in-VPC LRU caches, we can't have egress to external caches for PCI scope.
04:14 Elena: right, in the private deployment the KV cache is local to the pod/host, no egress. For the hosted runs we used internal cluster KV but we can replicate the VPC-local behavior for more realistic numbers — it'll only improve p95.
04:29 Maya: long seq? that's where we saw user complaints in prod with the incumbent last month.
04:33 Elena: long (512): p50 incumbent 1.1s, redwood 980ms. p95 incumbent 2.9s, redwood 3.2s — so on long sequences the incumbent marginally outperforms our current config at the tail. Throughput incumbent 40 rps, redwood 55 rps. Cost per 1k tokens incumbent $0.39, redwood $0.34.
05:05 Aaron: ok that's a surprise — why is your p95 worse on long seq?
05:09 Elena: couple reasons — our runtime favors batching and KV reuse which helps throughput and median, but for very long single-turn sequences the incumbent's runtime has special long-seq fused attention kernels that, in this model variant, edge out our tail. We have a plan to add a long-seq kernel variant and a fallback path for single-shard long requests.
05:29 Samir: and important to note the long seq path had small sample sizes in the trace; we'll expand the sample for the 2-hour stress to get more stable p95 estimates.
05:37 Maya: what's the risk if we canary Redwood with 5% traffic? will that spike error budgets?
05:42 Diego: our canary policy would route short sequences to Redwood first and leave the long seq to the incumbent while we monitor p95/p99 and KV hit rate — so the initial blast radius is minimized.
05:54 Omar: security — we need to see SOC2 docs and KMS integration notes. Also SSO (SAML) and RBAC mapping must support our AD groups.
06:03 Samir: absolutely — we'll attach SOC2 and ISO summaries and a KMS integration guide. We support customer-managed KMS via key wrapping and HSM integrations. SSO is SAML with attribute mapping — Elena will share details.
06:15 Aaron: do you have audit logs persisted to our SIEM? we need log forwarding and immutable audit for compliance review.
06:23 Elena: yes we ship audit logs and can set up a syslog/forwarder to your collector in the VPC; retention is configurable.
06:29 Jasmine: ok so next steps?
06:31 Samir: recap: Redwood sends raw CSVs and perf logs; Elena runs 2-hour stress test using customer sample and VPC-local cache behavior; Lyra shares KMS and VPC egress constraints; schedule canary design review for next week. Any other blockers?
06:48 Maya: pricing — we need a cost model for mixed routing (short on Redwood, long on incumbent) and a forecast for monthly spend at 5%/10% pilot. Can you sketch that?
06:58 Samir: yes we'll include a cost projection sheet when we send the CSVs. For the pilot we can provide an estimated delta and a configuration that targets parity or better on cost for medium/long by using a cheaper quantized variant on background jobs.
07:12 Aaron: on the kernel work timeline? long-seq kernel — how long until a test build?
07:18 Elena: engineer estimate is 3 weeks for prototype, 6-8 weeks to production-grade. We can backfill with a runtime fallback to incumbent for the tails during canary.
07:28 Maya: ok that's acceptable as long as canary has no user-visible regressions.
07:33 Samir: fair. Diego will coordinate canary metrics and SLOs.
07:37 Diego: i'll propose a metric set: p95/p99 per seq bucket, KV hit rate, error rate, and cost per 1M tokens. We'll send the template.
07:47 Jasmine: also want a short doc on rollback conditions — what triggers auto-failover back to incumbent?
07:52 Samir: we'll include rollback thresholds in the canary doc — e.g., p95 regresses >20% or error rate >0.5% above baseline for 5 minutes triggers automatic traffic cutover.
08:04 Maya: perfect. thanks everyone.
08:07 Samir: thanks — we'll follow up with the artifacts and set up the canary review.
08:11 Elena: i'll kick off the stress window on Thursday once we have the exact sample and VPC config.
08:16 Omar: i'll send the VPC/KMS details by EOD Wednesday.
08:21 Samir: awesome. Diego, please book the canary design review for next Wednesday 10am PT.
08:26 Diego: on it.
08:28 Samir: great, meeting adjourned.

Notes on transcription: occasional speaker mislabels and minor garbling; numbers reflect lab-run CSVs attached. Links shared in chat: perf-spreadsheet.csv (link), canary-metrics-template.md (link), SOC2-summary.pdf (link placeholder).
